newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks end higher, extending record run.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks end higher, extending record run.

text.p: U.S. stocks posted moderate gains on Thursday, with blue chips venturing ever farther into record territory.
The Dow industrials rose 29 points to 8117, the third consecutive closing high for the average. The S&P 500 and New York Stock Exchange Composite indexes also climbed to records.
The session saw stocks succumb to profit-taking pressure early in the day, only to rebound sharply in late trading as investors proved themselves willing to buy on even the slightest of dips.
The bull market offered a show of resilience today, with the Dow bouncing back sharply from a brief foray below 8,000 on continued strong volume.
"As the market goes to higher and higher levels, you have to show there's real demand for stocks to continue," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.
"We've been able to do that with record volume last week and more decent volume today," he said.
International Business Machines Corp was strongest among Dow components, gaining 2-3/4 to 107-7/8.

Early in the session, SoundView Financial analyst Gary Helmig raised his one year target price on IBM to $124 per share from $100, arguing that recent gains notwithstanding, IBM remained a relatively inexpensive stock.
While analysts acknowledged the market would eventually pause in its latest record-shattering run, few thought the current leg of the bull market was apt to reverse itself soon.

"This has been a very powerful advance the likes of which is very infrequently seen," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "There are many things coming into focus that make this market different."

Those factors include strong mutual fund inflows and corporate earnings growth, and an apparent green light from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, whose Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress this week dispelled fears of an imminent interest rate increase.
Also helping is a resurgent dollar, which soared to a six-year high against the mark and a 3-1/2-year peak against the Swiss franc on Thursday.

While analysts have cautioned a long-term strengthening of the dollar can hurt profit growth at U.S. multinationals, that effect is more than offset in the short-run by the increased investment flows it attracts from abroad.
Among individual issues, Digital Equipment Corp rose 2-7/8 to 42-5/8 after reporting fiscal fourth quarter profits that beat Wall Street estimates.
Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc surged 7-1/8 to 28-1/16 after agreeing to a $1.9 billion takeover bid from fellow medical product supplier Mallinckrodt Inc.
Mallinckrodt shares fell 1-1/2 to 38-1/4.
Microsoft Corp fell 3-7/16 to 138. At an annual briefing of financial analysts, the company said it expected its research and marketing expenses would rise in 1998.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.72 to 940.28, a record.
The NYSE Composite rose 1.80 to 487.31, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.48 points to 1569.13.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
